text.title: Frontend Design Variant Exploration Core Rules
text.summary: 22 testable rules grounding the Frontend Design Variant Exploration methodology. Non-negotiable rules for variant diversity, 3–5 ceiling, token persistence, a11y gate, and rationale requirement. Phase rules for requirements capture, brainstorm dispatch, refinement, and token promotion. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; the last rule binds the decision tree skip path.

rule.statement: Phase 0 MUST capture type + style adjectives + tech constraints in a one-page brief BEFORE brainstorming. Skipping the brief is rejected.
rule.rationale: Without a brief, variants drift everywhere; with one, divergence is bounded by intent.

rule.statement: Each variant MUST differ on ≥3 axes from every other variant (typeface, density, color, motion, layout grammar). Palette-only swaps are rejected as 'variants'.
rule.rationale: Exploration value comes from genuine difference; near-duplicates waste the exercise.

rule.statement: Each variant ships with a 3–5 sentence rationale linking its choices back to the brief. Variants without rationale are rejected.
rule.rationale: Selection decisions need explicit comparison surface.

rule.statement: Variants MUST be working code (runnable in Storybook), not screenshots / Figma mocks.
rule.rationale: LLM-generated mocks lie about what builds; working code does not.

rule.statement: Phase 3 MUST record the user's selection + rationale. Implicit selection ('we just used the first one') is rejected.
rule.rationale: future audits need the why.

rule.statement: Phase 4 MUST emit Storybook stories + typed component(s). Variants left as one-off prototypes are rejected.
rule.rationale: Without handoff, the exercise is design theatre.

rule.statement: Each variant lives in `designs/variant-N-<slug>/` with its own README + rationale. Mixed-into-src variants are rejected.
rule.rationale: exploration code must not pollute production paths.

rule.statement: Selection in Phase 3 happens against side-by-side renders of every variant at the target viewport, populated with realistic content. A decision taken from Figma frames or from source alone is rejected.
rule.rationale: Figma frames carry neither interaction state nor real content density, so the variant that wins on the artboard is routinely the one that breaks first at the real viewport with real strings. Rendering is also the cheapest place to discover a variant that does not build.
rule.reference: Renders every variant at desktop and mobile widths and stitches a comparison grid.

rule.statement: Design tokens (colour, spacing, type scale, radii, shadow) are extracted from the selected variant and named — primitive tier then semantic tier — before any production component is written.
rule.rationale: A component written before the tokens exist hardcodes its values, and every later rebrand or theme becomes a sweep across every component instead of an edit to one file. Extraction after selection is cheap; extraction after implementation is a refactor.

rule.statement: Storybook, its framework adapter and every addon are installed at exact pinned versions. Semver ranges (`^`, `~`) on any Storybook package are rejected.
rule.rationale: The Storybook ecosystem moves fast enough that an addon's floating range can pull an incompatible core major on a fresh install, breaking every story for everyone who installed later. Upgrades belong in scheduled, reviewable work, not in whoever ran `install` most recently.

rule.statement: Each finalised component ships in its own directory alongside its story and its test: `Component.tsx` + `Component.stories.tsx` + `Component.test.tsx`. Parallel `stories/` or `__tests__/` trees are rejected.
rule.rationale: Parallel trees rot the moment one side moves: the component is renamed and its story is orphaned in a directory nobody opens. Colocation makes a rename atomic and makes a missing story visible in the same listing.

rule.statement: Each brainstormed variant must differ from all others in at least three of: typeface, color palette family, density (tight vs airy), and motion style. Variants that share two of these are considered duplicates and must be regenerated.
rule.rationale: LLMs default to one "safe SaaS aesthetic" copied 3–5 times. Explicit diversity constraints force meaningfully distinct directions that accelerate human selection and surface unexpected solutions.

rule.statement: Generate exactly 3 to 5 design variants. Never fewer (too little divergence), never more (decision paralysis above 5). The ceiling is a UX constraint, not a budget constraint.
rule.rationale: Research on choice overload shows that more than 5 options reliably delays or prevents selection. The 3–5 range is the minimum for meaningful divergence and the maximum for actionable choice.

rule.statement: Persist each variant's tokens (color, type scale, spacing) in a local `designs/variant-N-slug/tokens.css`. Promote tokens to the global `tailwind.config` or `globals.css` only after the user selects a variant.
rule.rationale: Premature global token updates contaminate the project before a direction is chosen. Variant-local tokens isolate each option and make the promotion step an explicit, reviewable commit.

rule.statement: Run axe-core (or equivalent) on every variant during the brainstorm phase, before presenting to the user. Never surface a variant with WCAG AA failures.
rule.rationale: a11y failures discovered after selection require a redesign loop. Running axe per variant in brainstorm eliminates ineligible options early and avoids sunk-cost redesigns.

rule.statement: Each variant's README must include: audience fit, aesthetic levers used (the explicit diversity constraints applied), and trade-offs. A variant without rationale is rejected.
rule.rationale: Design without rationale becomes orphaned context in 6 months. Future agents given the rationale can extend the design consistently; without it they guess.

rule.statement: Each variant must be runnable as static HTML or a Storybook story. Reviewers must be able to click and interact, not read code. Non-runnable variants are invalid deliverables.
rule.rationale: Reviewers cannot evaluate typography, spacing, and motion from source code alone. Interactive variants prevent "looks great in code, terrible in browser" selection errors.

rule.statement: Before dispatching any subagent, collect: surface type (landing | dashboard | form | component set), style direction (minimalist | bold | corporate | playful), tech stack, and brand constraints. Do not brainstorm without these four inputs.
rule.rationale: Brainstorming without a style direction produces the average SaaS aesthetic. Explicit inputs become the diversity constraints that force genuinely distinct variants.

rule.statement: Dispatch `faion-frontend-brainstormer-agent` with explicit diversity constraints derived from requirements. Each variant goes into `designs/variant-N-slug/`. The prompt must forbid shared typeface, palette family, or density across variants.
rule.rationale: Without explicit constraints, LLMs generate one canonical design repeated 3–5 times with minor color shifts. The constraint prohibitions force meaningful divergence.

rule.statement: Present variants to the user with the comparison table. After selection, dispatch a refinement subagent with only the chosen variant's files — never the full brainstorm context. Re-quote the original spec at every refinement iteration.
rule.rationale: Passing full brainstorm context into refinement exhausts token budget and causes the agent to regress toward rejected variants. Context isolation keeps refinement focused.

rule.statement: After final approval, promote the chosen variant's tokens.css to globals.css or tailwind.config in a dedicated commit. Then dispatch `faion-storybook-agent` for stories and `faion-frontend-component-agent` for typed components. Never merge these into one commit.
rule.rationale: Token promotion is a design decision that deserves its own reviewable commit. Storybook and component generation depend on the promoted tokens; sequencing prevents them from using un-promoted values.

rule.statement: When the decision tree routes to `skip-this-methodology`, the agent MUST emit a structured `skip` decision (with reason + suggested-sibling) rather than running Frontend Design Variant Exploration under degraded conditions.
rule.rationale: decision-tree contract. The decision tree is the only place that knows the routing; skipping must be observable so the orchestrator can log the routed-elsewhere path.
